# First drawing session
Prepared 2026-09-16 for g-drawing. User reports fifteen minutes Saturday (request C); exact date/time not needed for this guide and not booked. Prototype plan; participation unknown.

Use your pencil and paper at a comfortable surface with one household object, such as a cup.

1. Minutes 0–2: place the object where you can see it; notice its overall height, width and outer edges.
2. Minutes 2–10: lightly sketch the outer shape. Look back at the object often. Add one or two visible details; an imperfect drawing counts.
3. Minutes 10–13: add a few parallel pencil lines to one darker area, then stop drawing.
4. Minutes 13–15: date the sketch and note: enjoyable, frustrating or mixed? Would you like another attempt?

Success for this session is a simple observational sketch plus your decision about trying again. If interrupted, a quick outline and one sentence about the experience are enough to report; no recurring commitment assumed. Return with what actually happened.

Exemplar: [National Gallery of Art drawing everyday objects](https://www.nga.gov/educational-resources/lesson-drawing-everyday-objects), inspected 2026-09-16. Transfer familiar objects, contour lines and hatching. Adapt the classroom exercise from multiple objects and six techniques to one object and two techniques within fifteen minutes; no special supplies or artistic-quality threshold. Timings are this plan’s estimates, not a validated training prescription.
